description: Team GWIN is a team of four from Bahrain. We built Luna: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, a free 3D browser game where players aged 7–12 explore the Moon and Mars and make the calls that keep their crew alive. Real NASA data drives the game: DONKI space weather, real asteroids and real gravity. Our skills: AI-assisted coding, game design, science research and storytelling. We'd welcome teammates who love coding, 3D design, motion graphics, animation or physics.
summary:
Luna: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a free 3D browser game that teaches players aged 7 to 12 how astronauts live and make decisions on the Moon and Mars.

Players walk their own astronaut around a Moon base and take on missions written by our team. Each one is a real problem, like dusty solar panels, failing life support or ice drilling. They pick from 2 to 4 choices on a timer and watch Power, Life Support and Crew gauges respond. A "Why?" card then explains the real science, with a link to a NASA source. Players also fly a hopper between field sites, pilot a rocket from the Moon to Mars, and climb Olympus Mons to switch on Olympus Station.

NASA data changes how the game plays. DONKI space weather sets how often solar flares hit. NeoWs supplies the real asteroids players dodge. Real Moon and Mars gravity controls jumping and fuel use. NASA imagery is used for the planets.

Up to four friends can play together online, with each crew decision made by vote. The game runs in any browser with no install or account, and a single-file offline version works without internet. That makes real space science accessible to students anywhere.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Luna is a 3D browser game where players aged 7 to 12 train as junior astronauts. They walk their own astronaut around a Moon base. A beacon leads them to each mission at the greenhouse, solar field, antenna and other sites. Each mission is a real problem written by our team, such as lunar dust on solar panels, failing life support, ice drilling or long polar shadows. Players choose from 2 to 4 options on a timer. Power, Life Support and Crew gauges change, and a Ripple view shows every system the choice touched. A "Why?" card then explains the real science and links to a NASA source.

Between missions, players fly a hopper to field sites and land softly on a pad. They pilot a rocket from the Moon to Mars, dodging satellites, debris and real asteroids. The story ends with a climb up Olympus Mons, camp by camp. The stars the crew earned decide how many lights come on at Olympus Station.

NASA DATA DRIVES THE GAMEPLAY

- NASA DONKI space weather sets how often solar flares hit during flights, and adds radiation and power stress on storm missions.

- Real Moon and Mars gravity controls how high the astronaut jumps and how much fuel the hopper burns (more on Mars).

- NASA NeoWs supplies the asteroids in the flight, with their real names, sizes and speeds.

- NASA imagery (LRO Moon, Viking Mars, Blue Marble Earth, Cassini Jupiter) is used for the planets.

- Every mission card cites a NASA article.

Saved data is always labelled as archived, never as live.

CREW MODE

Up to 4 friends join with a 5-letter code from their own devices. Each player has a role: Power Engineer, Life Support Officer, Flight Doctor or Mission Specialist. Every decision is a crew vote, which teaches teamwork the way real crews work. There are no accounts and no chat, and only the name each player types is shared.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Students learn real space science by making decisions and seeing what happens. It's free, runs in any browser and needs no install or sign-up. A single-file offline version runs from a USB stick, so schools with weak internet can still use it.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React, Vite, three.js (React Three Fiber, drei), Zustand, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion and PeerJS (WebRTC) for multiplayer. Every 3D model is built in code, and all sounds are made with the Web Audio API. Automated tests check the game logic and play through every flight. Hosted on Vercel, with code on GitHub. The code was written with help from Claude (Anthropic), an AI assistant. The concept, story, missions and design are by GWIN. No AI-generated images, video or audio are used.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Players don't just read facts. They live them, with choices that ripple through the whole base. Real space weather can change a flight, and real asteroids become obstacles. The game also includes moving around in low gravity and a summit climb on Mars.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Age 7 to 12: short, clear sentences, and each real term gets a plain explanation.

- Accessibility: reduced-motion support, keys 1–4 for choices, large buttons, and state never shown by colour alone.

- Low-end devices: a Lite 2D mode switches on automatically if 3D graphics can't start.

- Privacy and safety: no accounts, no personal data and no images of real people.

- Accuracy: every fact links to a NASA source.
Source code: https://github.com/haidermoulay3mk/luna

Play it: https://luna-swart-phi.vercel.app
